modeled_in: design basis (scale-up spec section 1): electrode gap, current density and both residence times preserved
justification: At equal current density and equal diluate and slurry residence times the salt removed per pass and the position-dependent resistances transfer directly from the laboratory cell; bench-to-pilot EDR desalting was comparable at equal current density and residence time.
source: Xu et al. 2021 (Membranes 11, 333); Rommerskirchen et al. 2020 (Desalination 490, 114453)

mechanism: Pumping of the diluate and slurry channels (pressure drop)
parameter: Water viscosity; Slurry viscosity ratio; Slurry channel diameter
justification: Laminar flow at the preserved gap and residence times: velocity = path length / residence time; diluate parallel-plate drop 12 mu v L / h^2 and slurry-channel drop 32 mu_s v L / D^2, compared with the 1.2 m static-head allowance already in the P1 and P2 pump heads (Static Head - FCDI-BES Modules); not added to the pump heads because both lie within that allowance (ratios in the processed ledger).
source_locator: Rommerskirchen et al. 2020 Fig. 11 (pumping energy at laboratory scale); FCDI-BES_scaleup_module_spec.md sections 2.2 and 3.2
note: Newtonian slurry estimate (no rheology measured); the processed ledger also reports a tenfold slurry viscosity

justification: Ohmic drop along the graphite plate for current collected from one edge over the full cell height, dV = J_eff rho L^2 / (2 t); added to the cell voltage. Wagner-number reasoning: the drop is compared with the 5 % flag of the scale-up spec (ratio in the processed ledger).
source: Newman and Thomas-Alyea 2004 (Electrochemical Systems, 3rd ed.); Pierson 1993 (resistivity)
note: graphite resistivity of order 1e-5 ohm m not checked against Pierson 1993 (owner action)

modeled_in: design basis: the operating point was measured over 41 d at the preserved geometry
justification: The laboratory operating point was sustained for 41 days at the geometry preserved at scale; an FCDI cell with 100 cm2 of active membrane area reached a feed-limited plateau current of 1.4-1.6 A (140-160 A/m2) at 60 g/L NaCl, a plateau the authors attribute to the salt available in the feed (1.65 A at unit current efficiency for the full desalination of the feed at 1 mL/min) rather than to an electrochemical limit; this is orders of magnitude above the current density of this process (ratio in the processed ledger). The margin on an FGD wastewater matrix was not measured.
source_locator: Rommerskirchen et al. 2020, full text p.8 (limiting current around 1.4-1.5 A for the standard system at 60 g/L, close to 1.6 A at low concentrate flux; 1.65 A for full desalination at unit current efficiency; Fig. 7 caption: active membrane area 100 cm2) and p.3 (Fig. 1: 100 cm2) (PDF supplied by the owner, 2026-10-06); FCDI-BES_scaleup_module_spec.md section 2.2 item 4
note: confirmed from the full text on 2026-10-06: the earlier sweep value (140-160 A/m2) had been read from the paper's current-voltage curves and is now stated as the paper reports it (1.4-1.6 A on 100 cm2); the processed ledger's 150 A/m2 reference is the midpoint of 140-160 A/m2

mechanism: Ionic shunt current in the feed and diluate manifolds
justification: Manifold shunt (leakage) currents of electrodialysis-type stacks: the total effective electrical leakage of electrodialysis stacks reported in the literature ranges from about 0.9 % to 12 % of the stack current (Peng et al. 2022, Table S1 of that paper), the ratio of leakage to total current in the authors' five-cell-pair laboratory bipolar-membrane stack was below 0.1 %, and leakage rises with the number of cell pairs and the current density and saturates (industrial stacks hold about 500 cell pairs); the shunt fraction raises the stack supply current and the power at the same Faradaic current.
source: Peng et al. 2022 (Sep. Purif. Technol. 290, 120816); Culcasi et al. 2020 (Desalination 485, 114450)
source_locator: Peng et al. 2022, full text p.1 (abstract and introduction: 0.9-12 %, Table S1 of that paper), p.3 (industrial stacks of about 500 cell pairs), p.7-8 (less than 0.1 % in the laboratory stack) and p.8-9 (cell-pair and current-density dependence, saturation) (PDF supplied by the owner, 2026-10-06); FCDI-BES_scaleup_module_spec.md section 3.1
note: confirmed from the full text on 2026-10-06; the earlier sweep statement '0.2-1.2 % of the total current in 25-50 cell-pair modules' is not in the paper and was withdrawn; the mode 1.2 % lies at the low end of the 0.9-12 % range and above the laboratory-stack value (values unchanged: an owner decision)

mechanism: Ionic and electronic shunt current in the slurry manifolds
justification: The carbon slurry is a percolating electronic conductor, so slurry manifolds carry an electronic as well as an ionic shunt; in the pilot module of Köller et al. 2024 the stacking units are independent FCDI cells that share one flow electrode, so the slurry forms a conductive path common to all cells (design evidence, not a loss measurement); folded into the same shunt fraction, whose mode is placed above the leakage measured in a laboratory bipolar-membrane stack for this reason.
source: Linnartz et al. 2020 (J. Membr. Sci. 605, 118095); Köller et al. 2024 (Desalination 572, 117096)
source_locator: Köller et al. 2024, full text p.2-3 (the stacking units share one flow electrode; Fig. 2 caption) (PDF supplied by the owner, 2026-10-06); Linnartz et al. 2020; FCDI-BES_scaleup_module_spec.md section 3.1
note: the 'insulated bore holes' attributed to the Köller et al. 2024 pilot on 2026-10-05 do not occur in that paper and were withdrawn on 2026-10-06; the shared flow electrode is cited as design evidence

modeled_in: folded into the current-density retention factor (Eq. S67)
justification: A uniform flow split was measured in a 5-cell FCDI stack (Yang et al. 2016) and current efficiency fell as membrane pairs were added (Ma et al. 2020); not modelled separately, carried by the retention factor.
source: Yang et al. 2016 (ACS Sustainable Chem. Eng. 4, 4174-4180); Ma et al. 2020 (Water Res. 168, 115186)

mechanism: BES internal and anode resistance growth with area
justification: Area-specific internal resistance grew from 11.7 to 19.7 mOhm m2 between 9 and 100 cm2 in a zero-gap MEC (Kim et al. 2026), and scale-up affects the volumetric current density of MECs (Jiang et al. 2023); at fixed voltage the current density falls accordingly, which the retention factor carries (membrane and electrode area scale as 1/retention). Kim et al. kept the maximum current density nearly constant with a flow path designed by hydrodynamic simulation, so the mode 0.59 is conservative. The lower bound rests on a threefold growth of carbon-mesh anode resistance from 10 cm2 to 1 m2, reported by Kim et al. 2026 citing Cheng et al. 2014. Independently, the 20-stacking-unit FCDI pilot module of Köller et al. 2024 transferred salt at 0.46-0.52 of the rate of the same group's 2-stacking-unit modules at the same feed flow per stacking unit (1.1 against 2.1-2.4 umol/(min cm2), at current efficiencies close to unity), a stack-level reduction of the order of the mode.
source: Kim et al. 2026 (Water Res. 294, 125503); Jiang et al. 2023 (Water Res. 241, 120139); Köller et al. 2024 (Desalination 572, 117096)
source_locator: Kim et al. 2026, full text p.1 and p.5 (11.7 and 19.7 mOhm m2; 25.1 and 21.7 A/m2) and p.2 (the threefold carbon-mesh anode resistance growth, citing Cheng et al. 2014); Jiang et al. 2023, p.1, p.4 and p.6-7; Köller et al. 2024, p.1, p.5 and p.6 (PDFs supplied by the owner, 2026-10-06); FCDI-BES_scaleup_module_spec.md section 2.4
note: attribution corrected (DESIGN_phase3 addendum A1): the 11.7 and 19.7 mOhm m2 are reported by Kim et al. 2026, not Jiang et al. 2023; value_type assumed; the threefold carbon-mesh anode resistance growth was confirmed from the full text on 2026-10-06 as a statement of Kim et al. 2026 citing Cheng et al. 2014 (it is in neither abstract and not in Jiang et al. 2023)

modeled_in: Eq. S29 and S49 (replacement NPV and life-annualised inventory; Materials Membranes Lifespan 8.5 yr, Monte Carlo 7-10 yr)
justification: Replacement capital and inventory at the membrane service life; component lifetime is a leading cost lever in CDI techno-economics (Hand et al. 2019; Liu et al. 2021).
source: Hand et al. 2019 (Environ. Sci. Technol. 53, 13353-13363); Liu et al. 2021 (ACS ES&T Eng. 1, 261-273)

modeled_in: full GAC replacement every six months (Materials GAC Biofilm GAC lifespan) plus Na2SO4 and sodium acetate dosing (Eq. S23-S24)
justification: Attrition was not measured; the design basis replaces the whole GAC inventory every six months and doses the electrolyte and acetate, which bounds the make-up from above.

The functional unit is the treated water (1 m3 of FGD wastewater treated); water moved into the flow-electrode loop changes the diluate recovery and the concentrate volume, a boundary effect (energy per m3 with and without water transfer in Rommerskirchen et al. 2020), not a cost or burden of the treated volume in this model.
source_locator: Rommerskirchen et al. 2020, full text p.5-6 (Fig. 5(b); sections 3.2-3.3: energy demand with and without the water transfer) and p.13 (Table: energy demand incl. water transfer) (PDF supplied by the owner, 2026-10-06); FCDI-BES_scaleup_module_spec.md section 6
note: stated, not quantified; confirmed from the full text on 2026-10-06: Rommerskirchen et al. 2020 report the energy per m3 with the water transfer included and warn that neglecting it underestimates the energy demand
